<!-- pr-reviewer: 7f528bebaacc48f2360fb30cd81772d6c546d436 -->

Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge. The review ran at the safety floor for a change to posted arcs (effort:high).

## Gate evidence

Built on the self-hosted runner through pr-test.yml: run 43593102443, main at ac1252979, trial merge clean. The run conclusion is `failure`. One ui test caused that. It is a known failure on main, not a fault of this PR (see below).

| Part | Result |
|---|---|
| Head check, read-only check, trial merge | pass |
| motion suites | ok - 46 binaries, 0 failed |
| app suites | ok - 43 binaries, 0 failed |
| ui lib | 771 pass, 1 fail, 5 ignored |
| clippy (app, motion, ui, all targets) | clean |

The one ui failure is `egui_app::tests::setup_mount_pages::each_setup_picks_its_own_machine_and_post_and_posts_one_file_per_mount`. It reproduces issue #1657, a real failure on main today. The warning text ("cuts past the finish surface" in a face op) matches that issue, not the contour arc fit of this PR.

The pinning tests ran on the merged tree and passed:
- `contour_arc_fit_wall::coarse_arc_fit_on_a_round_wall_verifies_clean_both_ways` (app)
- `arcs::a_sided_fit_never_passes_a_vertex_on_the_part_side` (motion)
- `law_tests::path_tests::arc_moves_draw_curved` (ui, now on `climb: true`)

## Checks

1. The law holds. `arc_side::sided` keeps the two-sided circle when every vertex stands at most `ARC_SIDE_SLACK` (1e-3 mm) on the part side. Past the slack, an open run slides the centre along the chord bisector (`one_sided`), and a closing ring is refused. A sided fit never posts an arc that passes a vertex on the part side.
2. Commit 7f528beba does what its subject says. True circles keep their exact arcs, so every golden posts unchanged. A refused closing-ring fit falls back to chords through the real vertices. The path then carries no arc at all, so no wrong arc is ever posted. The refusal has no separate log line. It follows the existing `Over::Fail` behaviour of the two-sided fit, and the verifier still reports any unsafe result. Noted, not blocking.
3. Goldens: the diff changes no golden, recorded, or snapshot file. All golden tests pass unchanged on the merged tree.
4. The pinning tests tell old from new. The app test fails on main (`Gouge { at: 3 }` .. `Gouge { at: 11 }`, recorded on issue #1579) and passes here. The motion test asserts the two-sided fit shows a part-side excursion above 0.01 mm and the sided fit stays within 1e-3 mm. Both files carry their `Gate map` header line. The app test imports commands, generate and verify from `crates/app/src`, so app is the lowest crate it can live in. The unit test sits in motion, the crate of the code it tests.
5. Prime Directive: no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` in the new code. Degenerate input is refused by returning `None`: a zero-length chord, a non-finite term, an empty feasible interval, a split vertex off the circle. Floats pass `is_finite` guards; the centre offset uses `clamp`. Index math is integer, with `.get` in `splits_on_circle`.
6. File sizes: `arc_side.rs` 130 lines; `arcs.rs` 399 lines (at the cap, not over); `contour.rs` 445 lines and already over before this PR, which is net-zero there.
7. Records: `docs/decisions/1579-arc-fit-one-sided.md` is present and complete (chosen, why, values considered, dropped options). `CHANGELOG.md` and `RECOMMENDED.md` are untouched.
8. The body carries a `Changelog:` line that matches the change, the commit subjects are conventional, and the body names the closing reference for issue #1579.

## What was not exercised

- The release heavy lanes and the pixel snapshots (release lane only).
- Windows arms of per-OS readings: the runner checked macOS. The diff adds no `cfg(windows)` reading, so no local arm was owed.
- A hand test in the GUI.

## Notes (not blocking)

- The slack (1e-3 mm) sits ten times under `GOUGE_TOL` (0.01 mm) and far above the rounding noise of a true circle. The decision record explains the choice and the dropped alternatives.
- `arcs.rs` now stands at 399 of the 400 lines. The next change to this file needs a split.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
